persons.note: REGRADED ON THE RATIFIED LADDER (T-0705, rule G1b): inferred -> attested. the rung above is reached on 3 appearance(s) across `newspaper_1833_1835`, `poll_1834`. The ladder's words for G1b: A contemporary record naming the person in Chicago — the 1833-1835 newspapers, which print the person by name in the town. — THE RECORD BELOW WAS WRITTEN BEFORE THAT RULING. HIS ADDRESS NAMES A STREET THIS PROJECT DOES NOT OTHERWISE HOLD. 'Main-street' appears nowhere in this dataset's street control, the Thompson plat module or either 1834 sheet, and it is a real 1833 Chicagoan's own word for where his shop was. The cross-reference is usable: Graves' Tavern is Dexter Graves's house, the log tavern on Lake Street that became the Mansion House at what are now 84-86 Lake Street. So 'Main-street' in November 1833 is very probably Lake Street or a stretch of it under a colloquial name. THAT IS A FINDING FOR THE STREETS LAYER, NOT A PLACEMENT, and it is recorded here rather than acted on. The Chicago Democrat of 26 November 1833 is the only contemporary Chicago document this project holds; an advertiser in it was paying to be found, which makes it strong evidence of existence and address in November 1833 and weak evidence of survival to 1 July 1835, nineteen months and about 2,400 people later. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Mason, Matthias” (poll_1834_070, line 239). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Mason' agrees with the entry's forenames; 1 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

research_note: THE ADVERTISEMENT THAT CONTAINS A STREET NAME NOBODY ELSE USES, which is the most useful thing in this household and has nothing to do with its people. A blacksmith is also the trade the inferred phase will need most of: a town of 3,265 with the wagon traffic Andreas describes could not run on the two smithies this dataset models, and this record is the documented proof of a third.
